messages:
matt: Quick heads-up — I ran the full traffic burnup sim for DayZero (prod profile + 3x spike) and pushed the results to the sim bucket. Need decisions on pre-warm window and reserved capacity.

jamie: Upload link? TL;DR numbers pls.

matt: Link: https://internal.sims/redwood/dayzero/1768204567  TL;DR: baseline QPS 9k, 3x spike => 27k QPS sustained for ~45m. Peak token throughput ~5.8M tokens/min. GPU-hours: extra ~420 GPU-hours compared to baseline for the 6h window (including 2h pre-warm). p99 latency crosses 400ms on current pool without pre-warm.

alec: 420 GPU-hours — assuming A100-equivalent? breakdown by region?

matt: Yes A100-eq. Breakdown: us-west2 ~60%, eu-west1 ~25%, ap-southeast ~15%. Cost delta ~$34k if we rely on on-demand; reserved + spot mix drops to ~$18k.

sophie: So what's the minimum reserved commit to keep p99 < 250ms?

matt: Simulation suggests reserving ~50 additional GPUs in us-west2 and 20 combined across eu/ap for the 6h launch window, plus a 12–24h pre-warm to populate KV cache. That gives p99 ~220ms. Without pre-warm you'd need ~30% more GPUs.

rachel: Pre-warm plan = synthetic requests or real replay? Risk of skews to metrics?

matt: Synthetic traffic that replays common prefixes + KV hits. We also suggested a short replay of last-week traffic at 10% mix to surface infra issues. Script: 

```
./burnup --profile dayzero --scale 3 --duration 6h --prewarm 2h --replay-week 10% --out sim-1768204567.log
```

Included KV-cache warmup step so model shards have populated cache before accepting real user traffic.

ops-forecast: Note: any reserving decision needs finance sign-off if cost > $25k one-off. Also need PO lead time for Dedicated pool changes (48h).

sophie: Can we shift some load to quantized variants to reduce GPU-hours? e.g., use 4-bit for non-critical routes?

matt: Yes — tiered fallback worked well in sim: routing 25% of gen requests to q4/alt models lowered GPU-hours by ~18% with +10ms latency cost. Recommending soft-routing policy during spike: 

- route by token-length: short (<64 tokens) requests -> q4 (fallback)
- canary threshold: if p99 < 300ms, increase q4 fraction to 40%

alec: Any networking hotspots in us-west2 during sim? We saw elevated RTT on one AZ earlier.

matt: Good catch. Sim flagged AZ-beta in us-west2 with sporadic 10–15% packet retransmits under load. For launch we should: 

1) avoid AZ-beta for critical shards (move replicas to gamma/delta)
2) enable cross-AZ read replicas for KV cache pre-warm
3) set routing policy to fail-over to us-west1/central if AZ-level errors exceed 5%

oncall-bot: deploy-bot scheduled: canary-prewarm/1768204567 -> will run at 2026-11-25T09:00:00Z (2h pre-warm).

rachel: Timeline constraints: marketing expects DayZero to be 2026-11-26 17:00 UTC. With 48h PO lead time, we need to decide today to hit reserved capacity target.

jamie: Proposed action list: 
- Approve reserving 50 GPUs us-west2 + 20 EU/AP (ops+finance) 
- Start 24h pre-warm tomorrow (synthetic + 10% replay) 
- Apply soft-routing fallback rules and q4 canary
- Evict AZ-beta shards and rebalance replicas to gamma/delta

matt: I second. I'll open the infra change PR and tag finance. If finance can't sign-off on classic reserved, ops-forecast: please run alternate spot+burst pricing calc.

ops-forecast: Running alternate pricing now; ETA 18m. Short note: if we do spot-heavy approach we need additional buffer for preemption — simulated that requires +12% GPU count to hit same p99.

sophie: Okay — tagging @finance and @product to confirm launch time. Anyone object to the plan? :thumbsup: or :thumbsdown:.

alec: :thumbsup: from infra.

rachel: :thumbsup: from product.

jamie: I'll prepare the PR and the runbook snippets for oncall. Keep replies short so we can lock decision today.

matt: Great — will paste the sim summary into PR in 5.
